scope: Frozen-model confidence evaluation on BRISC internal validation; not clinical validation

classifier.finding: The raw four-class and binary probabilities were already well calibrated internally. Neither temperature experiment produced a statistically stable accepted improvement.

segmenter_pixel.finding: Temperature scaling substantially improved foreground reliability but missed the fixed foreground-ECE gate and slightly worsened background NLL. The gate was not relaxed.

feature_provenance.source: raw segmenter probability map and unchanged 0.50 hard mask only
feature_provenance.reference_mask_use: target creation and evaluation only; no reference-derived model feature

calibration.baseline_definition: Each held-out fold receives a constant reliability equal to one minus the failure prevalence in that fold's training data.

bootstrap.unit: similarity groups resampled with replacement, retaining all member cases

strongest_mean_standardized_coefficient.interpretation: Higher boundary entropy is the strongest observed predictor of segmentation failure.

confident_wrong_signal.interpretation: A larger high-confidence foreground fraction can accompany lower reliability, operationalizing the confident-spatial-error finding.

interpretable_signals.limitation: The standardized coefficients are descriptive associations. Features are correlated and the sample contains 680 cases.

segmenter_case_reliability.final_all_validation_model_role: Proposed operational model for later integration only; it was not used for reported metrics.

cross_cutting_finding.title: Glioma remains the weakest subgroup
cross_cutting_finding.statement: The aggregate case-reliability pass is not uniform across tumor types. Glioma drives most segmentation failures and has the weakest reliability discrimination and calibration.
cross_cutting_finding.qualification: This does not invalidate the aggregate gate pass. It prevents claiming uniform reliability and requires explicit glioma caution in later use.
cross_cutting_finding.subgroup_metrics_role: Descriptive only; no per-category confidence intervals or predeclared subgroup acceptance gates were used.

what_this_work_establishes: The frozen classifier's raw probabilities are acceptably calibrated on the BRISC internal-validation partition under the declared gates.
Pixel temperature scaling improved several segmenter calibration metrics but did not satisfy the full fixed gate, so it was rejected.
Prediction-derived case features can rank Dice-below-0.50 failures in similarity-aware out-of-fold evaluation on these 680 validation cases.
what_this_work_does_not_establish: Clinical validity, safety, diagnosis, or autonomous use.
Patient-independent, cross-dataset, scanner-independent, or prospective performance.
Uniform reliability across tumor types; glioma remains materially weaker.
Guaranteed catastrophic-failure capture; 3/17 zero-Dice and 15/83 Dice-below-0.50 cases remain outside the top-risk quintile.
Acceptance of calibrated segmenter pixel probabilities; raw pixels remain in force.
Prospective performance of the final all-validation case model; reported metrics are out-of-fold.
Causal meaning for any reliability-model coefficient.

application_design_handoff.allowed_next_step: Design and validate the review policy that maps the score to display, warning, or required-review states.
application_design_handoff.required_qualification: The interface must preserve the glioma subgroup warning and must not present the score as clinical certainty.
